topics.title: Start a project
topics.summary: Create a local workspace and open a report.
topics.terms: welcome first project starter create open
steps: Choose Create project and select an empty folder.
Open an existing .amx file, or create one from the project explorer.
Edit the active document. Its preview follows the current unsaved text.
Use Inputs to map declared data, then Export to prepare a report or named data output.

topics.title: Starter examples
topics.summary: Begin with a bundled, offline report template.
topics.terms: example templates hello asset management operation note
steps: Choose a starter to create a project with a new report buffer.
The starter is saved through the normal conflict-aware autosave path; live preview follows the active buffer.
No explicit Run command is issued, and both templates use built-in values with no external files.

topics.title: AMX language essentials
topics.summary: Understand executable fences, imports, and typed inputs.
topics.terms: language syntax code fence markdown let type function import export input record table chart cli
steps: Only exact, case-sensitive ```amx fences execute; ordinary Markdown and other code fences stay narrative.
Use let for bindings, type and fn for typed records/functions, and input declarations for JSON or CSV data.
Imports resolve from local project files. Explicit exports control which bindings can be exported as JSON or CSV.
The desktop uses the same parser/runtime and preserves existing CLI behavior; this guide adds no alternate syntax.

topics.title: V0.12 language features
topics.summary: Use inherited records, enums, and braced conditionals.
topics.terms: language v0.12 record inheritance extends override effective fields enum enumeration primitive values braced if expression statement return AMX3011 AMX3021
steps: A record may extend visible record parents. Inherited name collisions require override; inheritance reuses fields and does not make the child assignable to its parent.
Without explicit enum values, numbering starts at 1. Explicit values must be unique Number literals or unique String literals of one type; member access returns that primitive.
The legacy if condition then value else value expression is unchanged. Braced if expressions require else and an explicit value return on every path.
Braced if statements may omit else. Branch declarations stay local, while assignments to existing outer bindings persist.

topics.title: V0.9 language features
topics.summary: Review V0.9 syntax and its compatibility changes.
topics.terms: v0.9 migration record constructor equals = colon annotation string escape interpolation list index dimension unit measurement conversion JSON CSV
steps: Record constructor fields use =; colons remain required for type annotations.
String escapes are decoded, and double-quoted strings support expression interpolation.
List indexes are 1-based. Dimensions, units, and measurements retain their declared identity and conversion rules.
Invalid programs are checked before execution. See the V0.9 migration guide before updating older documents.

topics.title: Documents and imports
topics.summary: Work with the active report and unsaved modules.
topics.terms: active tab import source editor save intelligence rename
steps: The active .amx tab is the target for analysis, preview, Run, and Export.
Open imported modules in tabs; current unsaved module text is used for analysis.
Save preserves exact text, including invalid drafts. Disk conflicts must be resolved before replacement.
Editor completion, diagnostics, navigation, and rename are derived from the shared parser and checker.

topics.title: Inputs and data editing
topics.summary: Map logical inputs and edit structured files.
topics.terms: csv json external private mapping schema validation
steps: Use the Inputs panel to browse for a declared logical input.
Project defaults are portable; local selections remain machine-local unless explicitly promoted.
CSV and JSON tabs support structured editing and raw text. Invalid source remains available for correction.
External data is labeled private. Diagnostic summaries never include its path or contents.

topics.title: Preview and export
topics.summary: Keep results tied to the current document state.
topics.terms: run preview cancel stale html offline interactive charts legend zoom static pdf data table docx json csv native editable embedded workbook numeric x line scatter markdown image link companion
steps: Preview updates after edits; Pause and Refresh are available in the context pane.
Run is explicit. A stale result is labeled and is not presented as current success.

Reports support headings, formatting, lists, tables, code, and visible source line breaks; authored raw HTML remains inert. Contained PNG/JPEG images need alternative text and are sanitized and embedded for offline use.

Charts are interactive in the live preview and HTML reports; PDF charts are static with complete data tables. DOCX uses native editable charts with embedded data when representable; numeric-X lines use straight-line XY scatter.

Unsupported axes, charts with no plottable points, and mixed-group scatter with a null-only group are deferred with a notice and complete table. A numeric-X line series with no plottable pairs is disclosed and retained in its table.

External links use HTTP(S). Supported contained local links are PDF, PNG, JPEG, TXT, CSV, or JSON, remain relative to the final report, and do not copy companion files. Word for the Web rewrites tested relative DOCX links, so local companion opening there is not claimed.
Export supports HTML, PDF, DOCX, JSON, and CSV where the selected binding is eligible.
Cancellation or a failed preparation preserves an existing destination; atomic replacement cannot be interrupted once started.

topics.title: Conflicts and recovery
topics.summary: Resolve external edits and recover unsaved work safely.
topics.terms: conflict autosave crash restore discard recovery
steps: Autosave writes exact text and pauses when an external disk conflict is detected.
Resolve a conflict before saving or performing dependent file operations.
Recovery snapshots are local and can be restored into memory or discarded.
Restoring recovery never writes over project files automatically.

topics.title: Diagnostic export privacy
topics.summary: Download a bounded diagnostic summary for support.
topics.terms: logs export privacy path secret credential source input
steps: The summary contains the app label, export time, coarse workbench state, and diagnostic-code counts.
It omits project and file paths, diagnostic messages, document/source text, input values, recovery data, and credentials.
The export stays on this device until you choose to share the downloaded file.

topics.title: Release notes
steps: The first public release includes a cross-platform desktop workbench, a command-line interface, and a VS Code extension.
Write computable documents with Markdown narrative, executable calculations, typed records and functions, local modules, and units of measure.
Create tables and charts, map and validate JSON or CSV inputs, and export results as HTML, PDF, DOCX, JSON, or CSV.
The desktop workbench includes live preview, explicit Run, conflict-aware autosave, local recovery, structured data editing, and report export.
